Impact of California Emission Standards
· .
Ford Motor Company. Ford calculates that the 6 percent deterioration in their California light truck fuel economy because of California's emission standard will result in a 0.1 mpg reduction in Ford's MY 1979 50-State light truck fleet average. Ford believes that the NPA AFES should be adjusted downward by 0.1 mpg.
Chrysler. Chrysler introduced the losses related to California standards in their response to the NPRM. Chrysler presented tables comparing the fuel economy results of the Federal fleet average (17.41 mpg) with the results for all 50 States (17.12 mpg). The reduction anticipated by Chrysler because of the deterioration in their California fleet is approximately 0.3 mpg.
Summary. Information from both manufacturers from analysis and test data clearly demonstrate a loss of average fleet fuel economy between California and the 49-State fleet. This factor is included in the range of environmental consequences set forth in the EIS.

Sulphate Emissions
General Motors Corporation (GM). GM commented that they did not expect an increase in converter size to meet the MY 1979 emission standard for light duty NPA's (0-6000 GVWR).
